_about: ¿Qué me recomienda?: Doña Carmen on her bench in the zócalo, in the afternoon (one set-up). 11 pictures: the hello, the lovely day, the tried-my-tip twist, food or sights?, what do you feel like?, hungry?, where are you from?, pointing across the square, the walk-with-you twist, anything else?, goodbye. Her tips themselves (the dishes, the places) are said, not shown.

items.prompt: Doña Carmen, a grandmother born and raised in Puerto Colibrí, sits on the green wrought-iron bench in the shade of the big laurel tree, about one third from the left, her hands resting in her lap on a small woven palm fan, looking up at the learner with a gentle, knowing smile ("¡Buenas tardes! ¿Le puedo ayudar en algo?"). Warm afternoon light; the kiosco soft in the background.
Change only her pose: she fans herself with the woven palm fan and tips her face up toward the bright sky, eyes crinkled with pleasure ("¡Qué día tan bonito!, ¿verdad?").

Change only her pose: she leans forward on the bench, one hand on her heart and the other half raised toward the learner, eyebrows lifted in eager expectation ("¡Ah, es usted otra vez! ¿Y? ¿Lo probó?").
Change only her pose: she holds both hands out in front of her, palms up, as if weighing two things, head tilted with a curious smile (somewhere to eat, or something to see?).

Change only her pose: she counts on her fingers, the index finger of one hand touching the fingers of the other, eyes turned up as she thinks of dishes, a delighted smile ("¿Qué se le antoja? ¿Mariscos? ¿Algo típico de aquí?").

Change only her pose: she pats her stomach with one hand and points with the fan in her other hand toward the arcades at the side of the square, eyebrows raised with a playful smile (hungry? there's good food close by).
Change only her pose: she turns toward the learner, head tilted, one open hand gesturing toward them, a warm, curious smile ("Y usted, ¿de dónde es?").
Change only her pose: she points with her whole arm across the square past the kiosco, looking where she points with a proud smile (something worth seeing).

Change only her pose: she is getting up from the bench, one hand on the armrest, the other beckoning the learner to come along, her rebozo over her shoulders, a kind, lively smile ("Yo voy para allá. ¿Quiere que lo acompañe?").
Change only her pose: she sits back comfortably with her hands folded in her lap on the fan, a satisfied, motherly smile ("¿Algo más, mijo?").
Change only her pose: she raises one hand in a warm goodbye wave from the bench, a broad, gentle smile ("¡Disfrute mucho Puerto Colibrí! Aquí me encuentra, en la plaza.").
